intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Sunrise Tour
experiences.description: Witness the breathtaking sunrise over the iconic Angkor Wat temple complex, one of the world's greatest archaeological wonders. Explore the intricate bas-reliefs and towering spires that tell the story of the Khmer Empire, with a knowledgeable local guide explaining the rich history and symbolism carved into every stone.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Beachfront Snorkeling Adventure
experiences.description: Explore the crystal-clear turquoise waters surrounding Koh Rong island, one of Cambodia's most stunning coastal gems. Snorkel among vibrant coral reefs teeming with tropical fish, relax on pristine white-sand beaches, and soak in the laid-back island atmosphere that makes this beachfront destination a must-visit.

experiences.name: Sihanoukville Seafood Market Culinary Experience
experiences.description: Dive into Cambodia's vibrant coastal food scene at the bustling Sihanoukville seafood market. Sample freshly caught grilled squid, Khmer fish amok, and spicy seafood soups prepared by local vendors. Join a short cooking demonstration to learn how to prepare traditional Cambodian coastal dishes using fresh local ingredients.

experiences.name: Kampot River Kayaking and Pepper Farm Tour
experiences.description: Paddle along the scenic Kampot River surrounded by lush mangroves and karst mountains, then visit a world-renowned Kampot pepper farm to learn about Cambodia's prized spice. Discover the cultural significance of pepper farming to the region and taste the unique flavors of fresh green, red, and black Kampot peppercorns.

experiences.name: Kep Beach Crab Market and Coastal Walk
experiences.description: Visit the legendary Kep Crab Market, a beloved Cambodian institution where local fishermen bring in their daily catch of fresh blue swimming crabs. Enjoy a beachside meal of crab cooked in Kampot pepper sauce, then take a leisurely coastal walk along Kep's quiet shoreline, exploring the charming ruins of French colonial villas that dot the beachfront landscape.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. After settling in, take a leisurely tuk-tuk ride to the nearby Angkor Thom South Gate for a short introductory walk around the iconic stone faces and bridge of giants — a perfect first glimpse of Khmer history without entering the main park yet.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pub Street and the Old Market (Phsar Chas) area for a vibrant evening stroll. Explore the night market stalls, browse handmade souvenirs, and soak in the lively local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick and affordable Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav) from a local street stall near the guesthouse for around $1–2 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khmer Kitchen Restaurant on Pub Street — a beloved budget-friendly spot serving authentic Khmer dishes like amok curry and lok lak for $3–5 per dish.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your Angkor Archaeological Park pass on this evening or early tomorrow morning. A 3-day pass costs $62 USD and is the best value for multiple days of temple exploration. Tuk-tuks from the airport to Angkor area cost roughly $8–12 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early (5:00–5:30 AM) for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise — one of the most breathtaking experiences in Southeast Asia. Watch the temple's reflection shimmer in the reflecting pools as the sky turns gold. Spend the morning exploring Angkor Wat's galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or tuk-tuk to the nearby Angkor Thom complex. Explore the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, then stroll through Baphuon Temple and the Terrace of the Elephants. End with a visit to the Terrace of the Leper King.
day_by_day.evening: Watch sunset from Phnom Bakheng hill (a short tuk-tuk ride away) for panoramic views over the jungle canopy and Angkor Wat silhouette. Return to town for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a baguette with egg and coffee from a local street vendor near the park entrance for $1–2 USD — a Cambodian-French colonial breakfast tradition.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic or buy fresh fruit and snacks from vendors inside the park. Coconuts cost around $1 each.
meals.dinner: Try Mahob Restaurant near the Old Market for affordable and delicious Cambodian home-style cooking — mains from $4–6 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and bring sunscreen and a refillable water bottle. The park is vast — a tuk-tuk driver for the full day costs around $15–20 USD and is highly recommended. Book your Phnom Bakheng sunset spot early as capacity is limited.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the jungle-clad Ta Prohm temple, famously known as the 'Tomb Raider temple,' where massive strangler fig and silk-cotton trees have grown over and through the ancient stone ruins. Arrive early to beat the crowds and enjoy the mystical atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Banteay Kdei, a quieter and less-visited temple with intricate carvings, followed by a peaceful walk around the Srah Srang reservoir — a sacred royal bathing pond with beautiful lotus flowers and birds.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap town (entry ~$12 USD) for a deep dive into Khmer civilization, history, and the stories behind the temples you've been exploring. The museum is beautifully curated and air-conditioned — a welcome evening retreat.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a traditional Cambodian breakfast of bobor (rice porridge) with ginger and fish at a local market stall for under $2 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the local family-run restaurants clustered near Ta Prohm — rice dishes with vegetables or fish for $2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vibe Cafe in Siem Reap — a popular budget-friendly spot with Western and Khmer fusion options, mains around $4–7 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Day 3 of your Angkor Pass — make sure you've used all three days wisely. Ta Prohm is best visited early morning (7:00–9:00 AM) before large tour groups arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning tuk-tuk to the Cambodian Cultural Village on the outskirts of Siem Reap. This open-air museum showcases traditional Cambodian village life, ethnic minority cultures, and miniature replicas of famous landmarks — a great cultural immersion experience for around $12 USD entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and boutique in town (free entry). Watch skilled Cambodian craftspeople carve stone, lacquer wood, and weave silk using centuries-old techniques. This social enterprise trains disadvantaged youth and preserves traditional Khmer crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Apsara dance performance — a UNESCO-recognized art form depicting celestial dancers from Angkor's bas-reliefs. Many restaurants offer dinner-and-show packages for $12–18 USD, including Koulen Restaurant or Smile of Angkor.

meals.breakfast: French-style breakfast at a local bakery — coffee and a croissant or pain au chocolat for $2–3 USD.
meals.lunch: Street food lunch near the Cultural Village — grilled corn, fresh spring rolls, and sugarcane juice for under $3 USD total.
meals.dinner: Included in the Apsara dinner-show package, or dine independently at a Khmer restaurant before the show for $4–6 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Apsara dance performance in advance, especially in November which is peak tourist season. The Artisans Angkor shop is a great place for authentic, ethically sourced souvenirs at reasonable prices.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Banteay Srei, located about 25 km north of Siem Reap. This 10th-century temple is often called the 'Jewel of Khmer Art' for its extraordinarily detailed pink sandstone carvings depicting Hindu mythology. The intricate craftsmanship is unlike anything else in the Angkor region.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return journey, stop at the Landmine Museum (free/donation entry), founded by former child soldier Aki Ra, to learn about Cambodia's devastating landmine history and ongoing demining efforts — a sobering but essential cultural and historical experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap and unwind with a traditional Khmer massage — budget-friendly options abound on Sivatha Boulevard for $6–10 USD per hour. Afterward, browse the Night Market for local crafts and street snacks.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your guesthouse if breakfast is included, or grab a simple rice and egg dish nearby for $1.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from the market for the road trip, or eat at a local restaurant near Banteay Srei for $2–4 USD.
meals.dinner: Try Bugs Cafe if you're feeling adventurous — a unique restaurant serving edible insects (crickets, tarantulas, scorpions) alongside more conventional Khmer dishes. Mains from $5–8 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Hire a tuk-tuk for the Banteay Srei day trip — negotiate a full-day rate of $20–25 USD including both stops. Banteay Srei is not covered by the standard Angkor Pass and has a separate entry fee of $5 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning boat trip on Tonle Sap Lake, the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Visit a floating village (Kompong Khleang is more authentic and less touristy than Chong Kneas) to see how thousands of Cambodians live on the water year-round.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the lake's ecosystem — spot migratory birds, flooded forests, and traditional fishing methods. Return to Siem Reap by early afternoon. Visit the Preah Ang Chek Preah Ang Chorm Shrine in the Royal Gardens for a look at local Buddhist worship practices.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Alley West (a quieter alternative to Pub Street) for local bars, live music, and street food. Enjoy a cold Angkor beer ($1–1.50 USD) and mingle with fellow travelers and locals.

meals.breakfast: Early morning — grab a takeaway coffee and sticky rice with mango from a street cart before heading to the lake.
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish served with rice and vegetables at a local lakeside restaurant near the floating village for $3–5 USD.
meals.dinner: Street food dinner on Alley West — try grilled skewers, banana pancakes, and fresh fruit shakes. Budget $4–6 USD total.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tonle Sap boat tour through your guesthouse or a local operator for $10–15 USD per person. November is a great time to visit as the lake is at its highest water level after the rainy season, making the floating villages even more impressive.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus or shared minivan from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approximately 5–6 hours, cost $6–10 USD with Giant Ibis or Mekong Express for a reliable budget option). Enjoy the countryside scenery along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh and check into a budget guesthouse near the riverfront (BKK1 or Riverside area). After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (entry ~$10 USD) — a stunning complex of golden spires, sacred Buddha statues, and manicured gardens that serves as the official residence of the King of Cambodia.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sisowath Quay riverside promenade at sunset — a beautiful stretch lined with cafes, restaurants, and locals enjoying the cool evening breeze. Watch the sun dip over the Tonle Sap and Mekong rivers.

meals.breakfast: Eat before boarding the bus, or buy snacks at the bus station.
meals.lunch: Stop for lunch at a roadside restaurant during the bus journey — $2–3 USD for a rice dish.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friends Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) near the riverfront — a renowned social enterprise training at-risk youth in hospitality. Delicious tapas-style Khmer food, mains $4–7 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Book your bus ticket in advance during peak November season. Giant Ibis is highly recommended for safety, comfort, and reliability. Store valuables securely during the bus journey.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison), a former high school converted into a Khmer Rouge prison where an estimated 17,000 people were tortured and killed between 1975 and 1979. This is a deeply moving and historically essential experience to understand Cambodia's tragic recent past. Entry fee ~$5 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk to the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (the 'Killing Fields'), located about 15 km from the city center. The audio guide (included in the $6 USD entry fee) provides a powerful and respectful account of the atrocities committed here. A memorial stupa filled with victims' skulls stands at the center of the site.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city and give yourself time to decompress after an emotionally heavy day. Visit the National Museum of Cambodia (entry $5 USD, open until 5 PM) to shift focus to the artistic and cultural achievements of the Khmer civilization — a beautiful counterpoint to the day's earlier experiences.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a Cambodian breakfast of nom banh chok (Khmer noodles with green fish curry sauce) from a local market stall for $1–2 USD.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Tuol Sleng at a local Khmer restaurant — rice with fish or chicken for $2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant, another social enterprise restaurant with a beautiful colonial villa setting, specializing in Cambodian countryside cuisine. Mains $5–8 USD.

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally intense. Dress respectfully and allow time for reflection. Tuk-tuk to Choeung Ek and back costs around $8–10 USD round trip. Consider hiring a guide at either site for deeper historical context ($5–10 USD).

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus or shared taxi from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (approximately 4–5 hours, $6–8 USD). From Sihanoukville port, catch a ferry to Koh Rong Samloem island (approximately 45 minutes–1 hour, $25–30 USD round trip) — one of Cambodia's most beautiful and relatively unspoiled islands with pristine white sand beaches and turquoise waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Koh Rong Samloem and check into a budget beach bungalow on Saracen Bay or M'Pai Bay. Spend the afternoon swimming in the crystal-clear water, snorkeling around the coral reefs, and relaxing on the beach. Rent a snorkel set for $3–5 USD from local operators.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the magical bioluminescent plankton phenomenon — at night, the shallow waters around the island glow electric blue when disturbed. Wade into the sea after dark for a truly unforgettable natural light show.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure in Phnom Penh — banh mi sandwich from a street vendor for $1–2 USD.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood BBQ on the beach — grilled prawns, squid, and fish with rice for $5–8 USD at a beachside shack.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant on Saracen Bay — fresh catch of the day with vegetables and rice for $5–8 USD, paired with a local beer.

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance during November peak season. Budget beach bungalows on Koh Rong Samloem range from $15–30 USD per night. The bioluminescence is best viewed on moonless nights — check the lunar calendar. Bring cash as ATMs are unavailable on the island.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a final sunrise walk along the empty white sand beach — arguably one of the most peaceful and beautiful moments of the entire trip. Take a last swim in the warm Gulf of Thailand waters and explore any remaining corners of the island on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Catch the midday or early afternoon ferry back to Sihanoukville. If time permits before onward travel, visit Otres Beach — a quieter, more laid-back alternative to Sihanoukville's main beach — for a final few hours of relaxation. Browse local souvenir shops for last-minute gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on your departure plans, either take a bus back to Phnom Penh (for international flights) or spend a final night in Sihanoukville. Reflect on an incredible 10-day journey through Cambodia's temples, culture, history, and beaches over a farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit platter and coconut from a beach vendor — $2–3 USD.
meals.lunch: Final island meal — fish amok (Cambodia's national dish, a coconut curry steamed in banana leaves) at a beachside restaurant for $5–7 USD.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Sihanoukville or Phnom Penh — splurge slightly on a nicer Khmer restaurant to celebrate the end of the trip. Budget $8–12 USD for a memorable final meal with Cambodian red wine or local Angkor beer.

day_by_day.notes: Keep $25 USD in cash for the Cambodia departure tax if flying internationally from Phnom Penh. Buses from Sihanoukville to Phnom Penh run regularly throughout the day ($6–8 USD, 4–5 hours). Book your return bus seat in advance. Overall trip budget estimate: $40–60 USD per day including accommodation, transport, food, and entry fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. Freshen up, then take a leisurely stroll around the hotel grounds and nearby Angkor village area to get your bearings. Visit the nearby Angkor National Museum (open until 18:00) for an excellent introduction to Khmer history and the Angkor civilization — a perfect primer before temple visits.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Siem Reap's Old Market (Phsar Chas) area for a relaxed first evening. Explore Pub Street and the surrounding lanes, soak in the atmosphere, and enjoy a welcome dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport meal)
meals.lunch: Grab a light bite at the airport or a quick stop near the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Cuisine Wat Damnak or Mahob Restaurant — both serve authentic Khmer cuisine at mid-range prices ($10–$20/person). Try amok (fish curry in banana leaf) and lok lak (stir-fried beef).

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or an ATM in town. Cambodia widely accepts USD. Purchase a tuk-tuk driver for the week (~$15–$20/day) — your hotel can arrange this. The Angkor National Museum entry is ~$12 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for sunrise at Angkor Wat (depart hotel by 05:00). Watch the sun rise over the iconic temple reflected in the lotus pond — one of Southeast Asia's most breathtaking sights. Spend the morning exploring Angkor Wat's galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Hindu epics, and the central towers. Your Angkor Pass (3-day recommended) covers entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a midday break and lunch, visit Angkor Thom — the massive walled city. Explore the Bayon Temple with its 216 enigmatic stone faces, the Baphuon, Terrace of the Elephants, and Terrace of the Leper King. Walk the jungle paths between structures.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up. Head to Siem Reap town for dinner and an Apsara dance performance — a classical Khmer dance tradition recognized by UNESCO.

meals.breakfast: Early light snack from a street vendor near Angkor Wat (rice porridge/baguette with egg, ~$2)
meals.lunch: Blue Pumpkin or Khmer Kitchen Restaurant near Old Market — sandwiches, salads, and Khmer dishes ($5–$10)
meals.dinner: Malis Restaurant — upscale Khmer cuisine with Apsara dance show included or nearby at Angkor Village Theatre (~$25–$35/person with show)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Archaeological Park pass (~$62 USD) — valid for any 3 days within a week. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) for temple entry. November weather should be pleasant and dry — ideal temple weather.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the remote jungle temples of the Angkor complex: start with Ta Prohm — the famous 'Tomb Raider' temple where massive strangler fig and silk-cotton trees have engulfed the ruins. The interplay of nature and stone is extraordinary. Then visit Banteay Kdei and the nearby Srah Srang reservoir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Preah Khan temple — a sprawling, partially restored complex with long colonnaded corridors and atmospheric jungle overgrowth. Then head to Neak Pean, a small artificial island temple built on a round island in a pond. End with Ta Som, a compact but beautifully preserved temple.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Pre Rup temple — a pyramid-style temple with wide open views, perfect for watching the sun dip over the Cambodian countryside. Return to town for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery near the park entrance ($3–$6)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a local market or eat at one of the simple open-air restaurants near the Angkor complex ticket area ($4–$8)
meals.dinner: Viroth's Restaurant in Siem Reap — elegant garden setting with refined Khmer dishes at mid-range prices ($12–$20/person)

day_by_day.notes: Today covers the 'Grand Circuit' of Angkor — hire your tuk-tuk driver for the full day. Start early to beat the heat and crowds at Ta Prohm. Bring insect repellent for the jungle temples. This uses your second Angkor pass day.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Banteay Srei — often called the 'Jewel of Khmer Art,' this 10th-century temple is renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings depicting Hindu mythology. Located ~25km from Siem Reap, it's a 45-minute tuk-tuk ride. Arrive early for the best light and fewer crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return journey, stop at Banteay Samré — a lesser-visited but beautifully preserved Hindu temple surrounded by a moat. Then visit the Cambodia Landmine Museum (free/donation) nearby — a sobering and important cultural stop that tells the story of Cambodia's tragic recent history and de-mining efforts.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Siem Reap, visit the vibrant Night Market (Angkor Night Market) for souvenir shopping — silk scarves, Khmer artwork, handmade jewelry, and local crafts. Excellent place to support local artisans.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café near hotel ($3–$6)
meals.lunch: Simple local restaurant in the Banteay Srei village area — rice dishes and noodle soups ($3–$5)
meals.dinner: The Sugar Palm — beloved local restaurant famous for traditional Khmer recipes using palm sugar and local herbs ($10–$18/person)

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is NOT covered by the Angkor Pass — entry is ~$5 additional. The tuk-tuk round trip to Banteay Srei costs approximately $15–$20. The Landmine Museum is deeply moving — recommended for all visitors to understand Cambodia's modern history.

day_by_day.morning: Use your third Angkor Pass day for the Western Baray and Ak Yum temple, then visit Phnom Bakheng — a hilltop temple offering panoramic views over the Angkor plain and Tonlé Sap Lake in the distance. Morning visits avoid the sunset crowds that typically overwhelm this site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon boat trip on Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Visit the floating villages of Chong Kneas or Kompong Phluk (the latter is more authentic and less touristy, ~$15–$25 for the boat tour). See how thousands of Cambodians live on the water year-round.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class in Siem Reap — learn to prepare 3–4 traditional Khmer dishes. Classes typically include a market visit, cooking instruction, and eating your creations. A wonderful cultural immersion experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Light snack on the boat or at the floating village ($3–$5)
meals.dinner: Eat what you cook in your cooking class! Most classes cost $25–$40/person and include the meal.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tonlé Sap boat tour and cooking class in advance through your hotel or a local tour operator. November is an excellent time to visit Tonlé Sap — the lake is at its fullest after the rainy season, making the floating villages most accessible. This completes your 3-day Angkor Pass.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siem Reap by early morning bus or domestic flight to Phnom Penh — Cambodia's capital and cultural heart. Bus journey takes ~5–6 hours (Giant Ibis or Mekong Express, ~$15); flight takes 45 minutes (~$60–$80). Check in to your accommodation in the city center near the riverfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the official royal residence featuring stunning Khmer and French colonial architecture. The Silver Pagoda inside the palace grounds contains a floor of 5,000 silver tiles and a famous Emerald Buddha. Then stroll along the scenic Sisowath Quay riverfront promenade where the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers meet.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively riverfront area. Visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco building from 1937 — before it closes. Enjoy dinner at a riverside restaurant watching the sunset over the Mekong.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at hotel or bus station café before departure ($3–$5)
meals.lunch: On the bus (pack snacks) or at a roadside stop, or grab lunch upon arrival in Phnom Penh ($4–$8)
meals.dinner: Romdeng Restaurant — social enterprise restaurant serving traditional Cambodian cuisine, staffed by at-risk youth. Famous for deep-fried tarantulas if you're adventurous ($12–$20/person)

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets in advance, especially on weekends. Giant Ibis is the most reputable bus company with comfortable seats and reliable schedules. If budget allows, the domestic flight saves significant time. Phnom Penh accommodation: a mid-range guesthouse or boutique hotel near the riverfront costs $30–$70/night.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge detention and torture center. This deeply important and sobering museum is essential to understanding Cambodia's tragic history under the Pol Pot regime (1975–1979). Allow 2–3 hours with an audio guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (Killing Fields) — located ~15km from the city center. This memorial site with its iconic stupa filled with skulls is a powerful and necessary tribute to the victims of the Khmer Rouge. Take a tuk-tuk (~$10 round trip). Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Cambodia — housing the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Evening at leisure in Phnom Penh. Explore the trendy BKK1 (Boeung Keng Kang) neighborhood with its mix of local and international restaurants, cafés, and bars. Visit the riverside night market if operating.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café ($3–$6)
meals.lunch: Friends the Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) — another social enterprise NGO restaurant near the National Museum, serving excellent Khmer and fusion dishes ($8–$15)
meals.dinner: Dine in BKK1 neighborhood — try Siem Reap Restaurant or a local family restaurant for authentic Cambodian home cooking ($8–$15/person)

day_by_day.notes: Today is emotionally heavy but historically vital. Take your time at both S-21 and Choeung Ek — don't rush these sites. Entry to Tuol Sleng is $3; Choeung Ek is $6 (audio guide included). The National Museum is $10. Be respectful and dress appropriately at memorial sites.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phnom Penh for Kampot — a charming riverside colonial town in southern Cambodia (~3.5 hours by bus, ~$8–$12). Check in to your guesthouse. Explore Kampot's well-preserved French colonial architecture on foot — stroll the Old Town streets lined with crumbling pastel buildings, local shops, and riverside cafés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Bokor National Park by tuk-tuk or motorbike — a mysterious abandoned French hill station at 1,000m elevation with sweeping views of the Gulf of Thailand. Explore the ghostly ruins of the old casino, the Bokor Palace Hotel, and the Catholic church, all shrouded in mist and jungle. The drive up is spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot town. Enjoy the famous Kampot pepper — the region produces some of the world's finest pepper, used in a popular local dish of crab with Kampot pepper (if in season). Relax along the Kampot River at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast before bus departure in Phnom Penh ($3–$5)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kampot upon arrival — Rikitikitavi or Epic Arts Café, riverside restaurants with great views ($6–$12)
meals.dinner: Rusty Keyhole or Ngor's Kitchen — local Khmer restaurants in Kampot known for fresh river fish and Kampot pepper dishes ($8–$15/person)

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is a relaxed, slow-paced town — perfect for decompressing after the intensity of Phnom Penh. Book buses from Phnom Penh to Kampot in advance. Bokor National Park entry fee is ~$5. Hire a local tuk-tuk driver in Kampot for ~$15–$20/day. Kampot is also famous for its durian farms if visiting in season.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kep — a small seaside resort town 25km from Kampot, famous for its crab market and beautiful coastline. Visit the Kep Crab Market at the waterfront — a colorful floating market where fishermen bring in fresh catches. Order fresh blue crab cooked with Kampot pepper directly from the market stalls — one of Cambodia's greatest culinary experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kep National Park — a forested hill with walking trails offering views of the Gulf of Thailand and Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) offshore. Take a short boat ride to Rabbit Island (~$5 each way) — a pristine, largely undeveloped island with white sand beaches, clear water, and simple beach huts. Swim, snorkel, and relax on one of Cambodia's most beautiful beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot by late afternoon. Enjoy a sunset kayak or boat trip on the Kampot River through the mangroves — a magical experience as fireflies begin to light up the riverbanks after dark. Many operators offer firefly tours (~$8–$12).

meals.breakfast: Café Espresso or a riverside café in Kampot ($4–$7)
meals.lunch: Fresh crab with Kampot pepper at Kep Crab Market — a must-do culinary experience ($8–$15 for a whole crab)
meals.dinner: Bokor Mountain Lodge or Café Aroma in Kampot — relaxed riverside dining with Khmer and Western options ($8–$14/person)

day_by_day.notes: Rabbit Island is best visited in the morning/early afternoon — boats return by 17:00. Bring snorkeling gear if you have it (or rent on the island for ~$3). The firefly boat tour must be booked in advance through your guesthouse or a local operator. November weather in Kep and Kampot should be warm and sunny (~28–32°C) with minimal rain.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kampot — visit a Kampot pepper farm for a guided tour. Learn about the cultivation, harvesting, and processing of the world-famous Kampot pepper (red, black, white, and green varieties). Purchase some pepper to bring home as the perfect edible souvenir. Then visit the salt fields on the road between Kampot and Kep — vast flat plains where salt is harvested traditionally.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Kampot for Phnom Penh airport (or Sihanoukville airport if applicable) for your onward journey. The bus/taxi from Kampot to Phnom Penh takes ~3.5 hours (~$10–$15 by shared taxi for a faster option). Allow plenty of time for your departure. Do some last-minute souvenir shopping at the airport or in Phnom Penh.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cambodia — carry wonderful memories of ancient temples, rich Khmer culture, moving history, and beautiful coastal landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast in Kampot — try num banh chok (Khmer noodles with fish-based green curry sauce), a beloved local breakfast dish ($2–$3)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch in Phnom Penh near the airport or a roadside restaurant en route ($5–$8)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Kampot pepper farms open for tours — La Plantation and Sothy's Pepper Farm are both excellent and bookable through your guesthouse (~$5–$10/person). Book your Kampot-to-Phnom Penh transport the evening before — shared taxis are faster than buses but slightly pricier (~$12–$15/seat). Confirm your flight departure time and allow at least 3 hours transit time from Kampot to Phnom Penh airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to boutique stay within Angkor Archaeological Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private welcome orientation at the hotel with a dedicated concierge. Settle in, freshen up, and enjoy a curated welcome amenity. Take a leisurely stroll through the hotel grounds and surrounding temple-adjacent gardens to gently acclimatize. Optional: brief guided introduction walk to the outer walls of Angkor Thom, just minutes from the property.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel terrace overlooking the ancient landscape. Private candlelit dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant featuring refined Khmer cuisine with modern presentation — think amok trey (fish amok), lok lak beef tenderloin, and mango sticky rice with coconut cream.

meals.breakfast: N/A — mid-day arrival
meals.lunch: Light welcome refreshments and afternoon tea arranged by the hotel upon check-in
meals.dinner: In-hotel signature restaurant — curated 5-course Khmer tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep pace relaxed. Confirm next-day temple permits and private guide with concierge. November weather is ideal: dry season, low humidity, pleasant 25–30°C temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private guided sunrise experience at Angkor Wat — arrive before 05:30 to secure a premium lakeside reflection spot. Witness the iconic silhouette emerge at first light with a personal expert archaeologist-guide explaining the temple's Hindu-Buddhist cosmology and bas-relief narratives. Champagne and fresh fruit served post-sunrise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive guided exploration of Angkor Wat's inner sanctum — galleries of bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk and the Battle of Kurukshetra. After lunch, visit the enigmatic Bayon Temple within Angkor Thom, famous for its 216 serene stone faces, followed by Ta Prohm (the 'Tomb Raider' temple), where ancient fig trees dramatically embrace crumbling stone corridors.
day_by_day.evening: Private Apsara dance performance dinner at a heritage venue near the park — enjoy classical Khmer court dance accompanied by a curated Cambodian royal banquet including steamed lotus-wrapped rice, grilled river prawns with kampot pepper, and banana flower salad.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn light bites and champagne at Angkor Wat lakeside; full breakfast served back at hotel upon return (~08:30)
meals.lunch: Exclusive picnic lunch arranged by the hotel within a shaded temple courtyard — cold cuts, tropical fruits, Cambodian sandwiches, chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: Private Apsara dinner show venue — Khmer royal banquet menu with premium wine and craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Temple passes must be purchased in advance (3-day or 7-day passes available). Dress modestly — shoulders and knees covered required for temple entry. Bring sun protection, comfortable walking shoes, and insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the lesser-visited but spectacular Banteay Srei temple — the 'Citadel of Women,' renowned for its extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest in all of Angkor. Arrive early to enjoy near-exclusive access before day-trippers arrive. Continue to Banteay Samré, a beautifully preserved 12th-century Hindu temple rarely visited by tourists.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Landmine Museum (established by former child soldier Aki Ra) for a poignant cultural and historical perspective on Cambodia's modern history. Afterwards, explore the vibrant Phsar Chas (Old Market) area in Siem Reap town — private shopping experience with a cultural guide to source authentic silk scarves, silver jewelry, and Khmer art from vetted artisan vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak — one of Cambodia's most celebrated fine-dining restaurants, helmed by Chef Joannès Rivière, offering a seasonal 5-course tasting menu rooted in Cambodian culinary heritage using local ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at hotel — eggs Benedict with smoked fish, tropical fruit platters, freshly pressed juices, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.lunch: Casual Khmer lunch at a curated local restaurant near Banteay Srei — fish amok, green mango salad, and fresh sugarcane juice
meals.dinner: Cuisine Wat Damnak — 5-course tasting menu with optional wine pairing (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is approximately 25 km north of Siem Reap — arrange private air-conditioned vehicle. Tipping artisans and local guides is culturally appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise hot air balloon flight over the Angkor Archaeological Park — soar above the jungle canopy for breathtaking aerial views of Angkor Wat, the Bayon, and the vast temple complex stretching to the horizon. Approximately 45–60 minutes aloft with a champagne toast upon landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided visit to Preah Khan temple — a vast, atmospheric monastery-city overgrown with jungle, less crowded than the main circuit. Continue to Neak Pean, an artificial island temple set in a sacred pond, and Ta Som, a compact gem with a spectacular tree-strangled eastern gopura. End with a tuk-tuk ride through the East Baray for a local village experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at FCC Angkor rooftop bar overlooking the Siem Reap River. Dinner at Malis Restaurant — a sophisticated celebration of Cambodian haute cuisine in an elegant open-air garden setting, featuring dishes inspired by royal Khmer recipes.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-flight snack provided by balloon operator; full gourmet breakfast at hotel upon return
meals.lunch: Riverside lunch at a premium Siem Reap restaurant — grilled Mekong fish, Khmer curry, and fresh coconut dessert
meals.dinner: Malis Restaurant — à la carte Cambodian fine dining with signature cocktails and local craft beer selection

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon flights are weather-dependent — confirm availability the evening prior. Book well in advance as slots fill quickly. Balloon flights typically depart at 05:30–06:00.

day_by_day.morning: Private full-day excursion to Koh Ker — Cambodia's remote jungle capital from the 10th century, featuring the dramatic seven-tiered pyramid temple Prasat Thom rising 36 meters above the forest canopy. Travel by private luxury vehicle (~2.5 hours). Explore with a dedicated archaeologist-guide the 30+ temples scattered across this UNESCO-listed site in near-complete solitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Koh Ker's outer temple clusters including Prasat Krahom (the Red Temple) and Prasat Leung. Enjoy a private picnic lunch prepared by the hotel amid the jungle ruins. Begin the return journey to Siem Reap in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel — private in-villa dinner or spa dinner experience. Enjoy a traditional Khmer herbal bath followed by a 90-minute signature massage at the hotel spa before a light private dinner served in your villa.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — continental spread with Cambodian porridge (bobor) and fresh tropical fruits
meals.lunch: Gourmet jungle picnic curated by the hotel — artisan bread, charcuterie, local cheeses, tropical fruits, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Private in-villa dining — chef-prepared 3-course Khmer dinner with herbal teas and dessert

day_by_day.notes: Koh Ker requires a separate entrance fee and is best visited with a knowledgeable guide. The road is paved and comfortable by private vehicle. Wear sturdy shoes — some temple climbing involved. Carry extra water.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer to Siem Reap domestic airport for a short flight to Sihanoukville (or charter flight/helicopter transfer to Koh Rong Samloem island) — approximately 1-hour flight. Check into a premium beachfront resort on Koh Rong Samloem's Saracen Bay, one of Cambodia's most pristine and unspoiled islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private snorkeling excursion by longtail boat to the island's coral reefs — explore vibrant marine life including reef fish, sea turtles, and hard corals. Return to the resort for a private beach setup with sun loungers, cold towels, tropical cocktails, and a personal beach butler.
day_by_day.evening: Beachfront sunset cocktails with live acoustic music. Private candlelit dinner on the beach — freshly caught seafood including grilled lobster, tiger prawns, and local reef fish with kampot pepper sauce, served with chilled white wine under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before transfer — yogurt, pastries, eggs, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachside restaurant on Koh Rong Samloem — grilled fish, coconut rice, and mango salad
meals.dinner: Private beachfront candlelit dinner — premium seafood BBQ with sommelier-selected wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Confirm flight/transfer bookings well in advance. Koh Rong Samloem has limited ATM access — carry sufficient cash. November is dry season on the island — excellent conditions for snorkeling and beach activities.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the private beach led by a resort instructor. Post-yoga, enjoy a leisurely breakfast on your villa terrace. Morning kayaking through the island's mangrove channels with a naturalist guide — discover the rich coastal ecosystem and birdlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat charter to explore the island's hidden beaches and sea caves on the less-visited western coast. Snorkeling at a second reef site, followed by swimming in a secluded lagoon. Return to the resort for a poolside afternoon with spa treatments — choose from hot stone massage, traditional Khmer massage, or a couples' treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail cruise aboard the resort's private boat around the island's southern tip. Return for dinner at the resort's premium restaurant — a sophisticated menu blending Cambodian coastal cuisine with international influences, featuring fresh crab, coconut-based curries, and artisan desserts.

meals.breakfast: Terrace breakfast at the villa — eggs your way, tropical fruits, freshly baked pastries, smoothies, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch aboard the private boat — gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, crudités, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — coastal Cambodian fine dining with craft cocktails and curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Full relaxation day — embrace the island pace. Bioluminescent plankton can sometimes be seen in the bay after dark — ask the resort about nighttime swimming conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Koh Rong Samloem — sunrise beach walk and a farewell swim. Check out after a leisurely breakfast. Private boat transfer to the mainland, then luxury vehicle or charter flight to Phnom Penh, Cambodia's dynamic capital city. Check into a luxury hotel in the riverside district (e.g., Raffles Hotel Le Royal or Rosewood Phnom Penh).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — marvel at the Throne Hall's gilded spires, the Emerald Buddha, and the 5,000 silver floor tiles of the Silver Pagoda. Continue to the National Museum of Cambodia, home to the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts spanning 1,500 years of civilization.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktails at the Elephant Bar at Raffles Hotel Le Royal — a legendary colonial institution frequented by Somerset Maugham and Jackie Kennedy. Dinner at Malis Phnom Penh — the capital's outpost of Cambodia's premier fine-dining brand, set in a stunning heritage villa.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Riverside lunch in Phnom Penh upon arrival — fresh spring rolls, lok lak, and Cambodian iced coffee at a premium riverside restaurant
meals.dinner: Malis Phnom Penh — Khmer fine dining in a heritage villa setting with signature cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Phnom Penh is a vibrant, fast-paced city — a contrast to the island and temple experiences. Arrange private transfers throughout. The Royal Palace is closed on certain public holidays — confirm opening hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply moving and essential historical site documenting the Khmer Rouge atrocities of 1975–1979. Continue to the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (Killing Fields) for a comprehensive understanding of Cambodia's tragic recent history. A knowledgeable guide provides context and ensures a respectful, informed experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Decompression time at the hotel spa following the emotionally significant morning. Afternoon visit to the Phnom Penh riverside promenade — stroll along the Tonlé Sap and Mekong confluence. Explore the Psar Thmei (Central Market) Art Deco building for premium Cambodian crafts, silks, and gemstones with a personal shopping guide.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails aboard a private riverboat cruise along the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers — watch the city's golden skyline at dusk with canapés and champagne. Dinner at Topaz Restaurant — Phnom Penh's most celebrated French-Cambodian fine-dining establishment, offering an exquisite fusion tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — extensive buffet with live cooking stations, fresh juices, and Cambodian breakfast specialties
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a riverside café — Cambodian noodle soup (kuy teav), fresh rolls, and tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Topaz Restaurant — French-Cambodian tasting menu with sommelier-curated wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — allow time for reflection. Photography is permitted but should be handled with sensitivity. Private guides help provide essential historical and cultural context.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cambodia — leisurely hotel breakfast. Private guided visit to Wat Phnom, the hilltop temple that gives Phnom Penh its name, for a peaceful final cultural moment. Browse the boutique galleries along Street 240 for last-minute premium souvenirs — silk paintings, lacquerware, and contemporary Cambodian art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell lunch at a top riverside restaurant. Final hotel check-out with private luxury transfer to Phnom Penh International Airport. Allow ample time for premium lounge access and departure formalities.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the memories of ancient temples, pristine beaches, profound history, and extraordinary Khmer culture.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final hotel breakfast — full spread with Cambodian and international options, fresh juices, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a premium Phnom Penh riverside restaurant — grilled seafood, Khmer curry, fresh fruit, and a farewell cocktail
meals.dinner: In-flight or at airport lounge

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for international flights from Phnom Penh. Confirm baggage allowance for any artisan purchases or silk items acquired during the trip. USD is widely accepted throughout Cambodia — settle any outstanding balances before departure.
